about.title: San Pablo Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a death happens because of someone else's carelessness — whether on I-80, San Pablo Avenue, Rumrill Boulevard, or elsewhere in the city — surviving family members are often left sorting through grief and unanswered questions at the same time. California law gives certain relatives and dependents the right to pursue a wrongful death claim, but that right comes with a strict two-year filing deadline (shorter if a government agency is involved, which can matter given San Pablo's city-maintained roads). LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we're a free service that connects grieving families with an independent attorney who can review what happened, explain your options, and handle the legal work on a contingency basis. You focus on your family. We focus on getting you in front of someone who can help you understand where you stand under California law.

whyChoose.title: Why Families in San Pablo Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Standing Rules Are Specific
items.desc: California limits who can file a wrongful death claim, generally starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children before extending to other dependents. An attorney can quickly tell you whether you qualify and who else may need to be included.

items.title: The Clock Starts Right Away
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of death to file, but that window shortens significantly if a government entity — such as the city of San Pablo — may be responsible. Getting matched with an attorney sooner rather than later helps protect that deadline.

items.title: Losses Go Beyond Funeral Costs
items.desc: California law allows families to seek recovery for lost financial support and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance, not just funeral and burial expenses. An independent attorney can help you understand the full scope of what may be claimed.

items.question: Who in my family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Typically, a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have the first right to file. If none of those exist, other dependents or heirs may be able to bring the claim. An attorney can review your family's specific situation to confirm who has standing.

items.question: San Pablo's recent crash data shows no traffic deaths last year — does that mean wrongful death claims don't apply here?
items.answer: Not at all. Wrongful death claims can arise from many kinds of incidents beyond traffic collisions, including workplace accidents, falls, or medical negligence, and fatal crashes can still happen even in years with lower reported counts. If your family has lost someone under circumstances you believe were preventable, it's worth having an attorney review the facts.

items.question: How long do we have to take legal action after a death?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit, but that period is shorter if a government agency, like a city road department, may share responsibility. Because evidence and witness memories fade quickly, connecting with an attorney early gives your family more options.
